phase_0.boundary_condition: The corrected operation table (Corpus Belnap) containing the truth-order lattice where N and B are incomparable, enclosing the migration of proofs from the divergent Root table.

⊢.justification: The uninitialized state of the system before migration, where N is absorbing for conjunction and B is absorbing for disjunction, creating a priority reading that contradicts the truth-order lattice.

⊣.justification: The terminal anchor defining the closed boundary of the corrected system where N and B are incomparable, enforcing the standard truth-order meet and join.

≻.justification: The directed transformation moving proofs from the divergent table toward the corrected table, preserving integer winding invariants.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism that identifies and retracts proofs that were true only under the divergence, collapsing them to the classical fragment or falsity.

⋈.justification: The sequential chaining of proof steps that must be re-evaluated under the new operation table to ensure geometric consistency.

⊙.justification: The identity of the Gödel sentence within the system, which remains invariant under the migration as it drives all states to B.

∈.justification: The branching point where a theorem is evaluated under both the divergent table (T-arm) and the corrected table (F-arm) to determine survival.

∋.justification: The rejoining of the evaluation arms into a single B4 verdict, where conflicting results (survival vs. failure) fuse to B.

⊤.justification: The affirmative evaluation of a proof that survives unchanged under the corrected table, such as the Frobenius closure theorem.

⊥.justification: The negative evaluation of a proof that fails under the corrected table because it relied on the divergent absorbing properties of N or B.

⊞.justification: The paradice state where a proof is both true (under divergence) and false (under correction), held simultaneously as B without resolution.

◻.justification: The permanent, append-only record of the migrated theorem in the corrected table, fixing the new truth value.

phase_3.void_description: The state before any operation table is defined, where no truth values exist.
phase_3.true_description: A proof that survives migration unchanged, such as the Frobenius closure theorem which holds in both tables.
phase_3.false_description: A proof that fails under the corrected table because it relied on the divergent absorbing properties of N or B.
phase_3.both_description: A proof that is true under the divergent table but false under the corrected table, held as a contradiction (B) without explosion.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the system with the divergent root table where N is absorbing for conjunction.
Fork the evaluation of a theorem into two arms: one under the divergent table, one under the corrected table.
Move the T-arm forward to evaluate the theorem under the corrected table.
Affirm the survival of the theorem if it holds under the corrected table (e.g., Frobenius closure).
Move the F-arm backward to evaluate the theorem under the divergent table.
Negate the survival of the theorem if it fails under the corrected table (e.g., N ∧ B = N vs F).
Hold the contradictory state where the theorem is both true (divergent) and false (corrected).
Rejoin the T-arm and F-arm into a single B4 verdict, fusing the conflict to B.
Chain the migrated theorem with other proofs to ensure geometric consistency.
Self-reference the Gödel sentence, which remains invariant as it drives all states to B.
Permanently record the migrated theorem in the corrected table.
Anchor the system in the corrected table, closing the migration process.
